```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = '#>', eval = FALSE)
```

Some generated wrappers accept a whole vector in one call. This guide is for the
person calling such a wrapper. The maintainer who enables batching on an
operation should read [configuration](configuration.html#many-inputs-in-one-call-fan_out-and-split)
instead. The examples use a hypothetical client with two batched wrappers.

## The two shapes

A **fan-out** wrapper takes a vector for one argument and sends one request per
element:

```{r fan-out}
get_item(c('A', 'B', 'C'))   # three GET requests: /items/A, /items/B, /items/C
```

A **split** wrapper takes a long array as its body and sends it in chunks of at
most the size the API accepts:

```{r split}
bulk_search(ids)             # for 450 ids and a limit of 200: three POST requests
```

Both send their requests one after another, in input order. Every other argument
is the same on every request. A single value, or a vector that fits in one
request, sends one request. For a fan-out wrapper every element is checked against the argument's
schema before anything is sent, so a bad element fails the call without any
partial traffic. A split body is checked as a whole first; the API's size limits
are then checked on each chunk as it is sent. The wrapper's help page says which argument takes a vector.

## What you get back

The results of all requests are combined into one value, so `get_item('A')` and
`get_item(c('A', 'B'))` have the same shape:

- Responses that are records come back as one list of records, in request order.
  A single record is still a list of length one: `get_item('A')` returns
  `list(record)`, not `record`.
- If the client turns responses into a table, you get one table for the whole
  call. Column types are worked out once, over all the rows, exactly as they
  would be if the API had returned every row in a single response. (If a hook
  edits the table after it is built, or the requests built their tables with
  different options, the tables are stacked as they are instead.) A column of
  `"F"` values in one request and `"MF"` in another stays text, and an identifier
  such as `"007"` is treated the same in every row.
- A `query` column, when the client provides one, names the input each row came
  from.
- A request that returns nothing adds no rows. It is not an error.

## When a request fails

By default the first failed request stops the call with its error, and nothing
is returned. A client can instead be set to **drop** failures. Each failure then
gives a warning naming its input, and the other results are returned:

```{r failures}
x <- get_item(c('A', 'missing', 'C'))
#> Warning message:
#> Request for missing failed: HTTP 404 application/json response
attr(x, 'failed')
#>                                  missing
#> "HTTP 404 application/json response"
```

`attr(x, 'failed')` maps each failed input to its error message; it is absent
when everything succeeded. For a split wrapper a chunk fails as a whole, so the
name is that chunk's items joined with `, `. Retry only what failed:

```{r retry}
failed <- attr(x, 'failed')
if (length(failed)) retry <- get_item(names(failed))
```

Problems that affect the whole call are never dropped. A missing credential, an
invalid option or an unresolvable server raises one error straight away, before
any request, whichever way failures are set.

## Choose how failures behave

The client's default can be overridden for the current session. The option name
is your package's option prefix, the request helper's name and `.batching`; ask
the client's maintainer for the exact name:

```{r option}
options(mypackage.api_request.batching = list(on_error = 'stop'))  # fail fast
options(mypackage.api_request.batching = list(on_error = 'drop'))  # keep going
```

## Wrappers that return many pages

A different kind of wrapper fetches every page of one result. It has `all_pages`
and `max_pages` arguments and is described in [Fetch every page of a
result](paged-wrappers.html). A wrapper does one or the other, never both.

## If you need more control

`specmill::batched(fn, items, size, ...)` is a manual tool for splitting any
call into chunks yourself. It returns the unmerged list of results, and errors
propagate. Generated wrappers do not use it for you; they use the settings above.

Maintainers: per-request and whole-result hooks are described in
[hooks](hooks.html#run-a-hook-on-the-combined-result-of-a-batched-wrapper).
